events.title: This Wild Life
events.description: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, moves to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. It is the busiest week of the season at the safari camp, and Saba is on a mission to find newborn lion cubs. Husband Frank races to rescue a lioness in need of help. A power crisis strikes camp, and a member of the team is rushed to the hospital with suspected malaria. Can Saba and Frank keep their dream alive and the guests happy during their busiest week so far? Participant - Saba Douglas-Hamilton Participant - Frank Pope Narrator - Julian Rhind-Tutt Series Producer - Susanna Handslip Executive Producer - Ted Oakes Director - Joe Keenan.

events.title: Prayer and Reflection
events.description: Prayer and reflection from the Palpung Changchub Dargyeling Tibetan Buddhist centre in Brynmawr, led by Choje Lama Rabsang. We join the centre for a traditional puja, a devotional practice that includes prayers, chants and mantras in Tibetan. The puja aims to develop an enlightened vision of the world. It is a form of meditation accompanied by intense visualisation that cultivates mindfulness, compassion and wisdom. This puja is dedicated to Guru Rinpoche or Precious Teacher, a Buddhist master from the 8th century, who is considered the Second Buddha in Tibetan Buddhism and is known as one who removes obstacles. He is said to have been born from a lotus flower. Prayers to Guru Rinpoche are considered to be increasingly potent during difficult times, and he is often invoked for protection. The puja practice helps to avert spiritual obstacles and pacifies all negativity on the path to enlightenment. events.title: Songs of Praise
events.description: Sean Fletcher is in London to meet young footballing superstar and proud England Lioness Michelle Agyemang as she shares her remarkable journey of faith. At her family church, Michelle reflects on how faith has shaped her life from an early age and become the foundation of both her career and her values. She explains why sharing the gospel is so important to her and why music remains central to her worship, even treating Sean to a favourite hymn on the piano. The journey continues to the Emirates Stadium, home to Arsenal FC. An Arsenal fan since the age of six, Michelle reflects on her footballing journey, her crucial goals at the Euros and the injury that threatened to derail her progress. She shares how her faith has given her strength, resilience and purpose both on and off the pitch. With music chosen by Michelle to reflect her faith journey. 1. You Are Good – House on the Rock, London 2. Total Praise – Sound Foundation Choir3. Because He Lives – Charlotte Chapel, Edinburgh4. The Old Rugged Cross – St Thomas’ Newcastle5. In Christ Alone – Unoma Okudo6. Ancient of Days – Liverpool Olympia Presenter - Sean Fletcher Producer - Ross Blair Producer - David Waters Executive Producer - Naomi Callan Executive Producer - Caroline Matthews Production Company - CTVC.

events.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
events.description: Third-generation farmer Alan is retiring, and with no-one to inherit the family farm, he’s selling up. Before the land can be sold, he needs to empty his farmhouse, four barns and several outbuildings of furniture, heirlooms and machines. After 60 years of working the land and wrestling sheep, Alan is looking forward to spending more time with his family and is hoping for a field day with his everything-must-go sale. Can he harvest enough cash to renovate an old cottage so his loved ones can visit him? Auctioneer Christina Trevanion has just one day to separate the wheat from the chaff and find items worthy of going under her gavel. She gains some traction when she finds collectable vintage toys in the loft, Second World War gas masks in the bedroom and an unusual machine that could be worth a fortune in the hallway. JJ goes whole hog on restoring a barn as he takes a huge risk on the rust - there’s a chance he could damage the object beyond repair. However, with Christina’s advice ringing in his ears, JJ handles a rare 1940s bell with kid gloves. On auction day, everyone is hoping for good chimes when the old bell sells, but the unlikely star lot is the sole survivor of a bygone age on the farm... a sock-making machine. Presenter - Christina Trevanion Presenter - JJ Chalmers Series Producer - Julie Grant Executive Producer - John Redshaw Production Company - STV Productions.

events.title: Garden Rescue
events.description: Chris Hull and Lee Burkhill travel to Coventry to help Amy, Ryan and their family transform their disorganised, outdated garden into a sporty, modern haven for everyone to enjoy. The current space lacks structure, with tired decking, no clear play area for the kids and little visual appeal near the house. The family dream of a modern, low-maintenance and dog-friendly garden, a place to relax, eat and spend time together. Reflecting the children’s love of weight training, gymnastics and football, the design will feature a sport-inspired theme, complete with a sunken seating area and a fire pit for cosy evenings. They also hope to include a special space to honour the memory of Lily Mae, the daughter they sadly lost at birth. Parents Amy and Ryan juggle life with their five sport-mad children and run a charity supporting families who have experienced baby loss. Now, they are hoping for a garden that balances energy and calm, a sanctuary where they can stay active, unwind and create lasting memories together. Can Chris and Lee craft a family-friendly, sport-inspired garden on a £5,000 budget? events.title: Bargain Hunt
events.description: What do Lord's Cricket Pavilion, Glasgow’s Ibrox Stadium and Liverpool University have in common? They are all constructed with distinctive terracotta tiles and bricks made by JC Edwards in the north Wales town of Wrexham. The company even made tiles for the ocean liners, Titanic and Olympic! In the 19th century, this Welsh firm employed more than a thousand people, making high-quality bricks for some of the nation’s most famous buildings, and local historian Phil Vaughan is keen to show Roo Irvine JC Edwards’s architectural legacy. Hoping to construct a profit are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for deals in the Herefordshire market town of Leominster. On the red team are friends Tracey and Hilary, who met while teaching in school. They are up against pals Julia and Helen on the blue team. With antiques expert Charles Hanson by their side, the red team have their heads turned by a ceramic owl. The blues, meanwhile, are on a giraffe hunt. Their expert Richard Madley thinks a silver-plated one has legs! Back in Wrexham, auctioneer Matthew Tong gives his estimates on the teams’ items, and for one duo, there is a blooming marvellous bonus buy! Presenter - Roo Irvine Expert - Charles Hanson Expert - Richard Madley Production Manager - Moira Edwards Executive Producer - Paul Tucker Series Producer - Joanne Dunscombe Director - Simon Brant.
